candidates.support: Wikidata's coordinate for the ridge is corroborated by OpenBible.info's independently recorded point for the same feature.

summary.text: The Mount of Olives is the ridge overlooking Jerusalem's Old City from the east across the Kidron Valley, described in the Gospels as a place Jesus and his disciples regularly visited, including on the night before his arrest.

otConnections.note: Zechariah's prophecy that 'his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives' on a coming day of the Lord is widely noted as background for the mount's later Jewish and Christian eschatological associations.
David's flight over the Mount of Olives during Absalom's revolt is the earliest narrative use of the mountain as a named place on a route out of Jerusalem.
